name: Peripheral Polyneuropathy
definition: Diffuse peripheral nerve disorder, commonly length-dependent, causing sensory, motor and/or autonomic dysfunction. Diabetes is common but metabolic, toxic, nutritional, immune and hereditary causes also occur.

typical: Weakness or autonomic symptoms in more advanced/atypical disease

redFlags.item: Marked asymmetry or predominant motor weakness

investigations.principle: Evaluation should be cause-directed and guided by pattern.
investigations.MRI: MRI is not routine for typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy but may assess suspected root/cord disease.
investigations.radiographs: Electrodiagnostic testing is useful for atypical, motor, asymmetric or diagnostically uncertain cases.

amber: Neuropathic-pain medicines and further laboratory/electrodiagnostic testing require individualized assessment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Individualized Vata/Dhatu/Srotas assessment may be documented in parallel; cause-specific modern diagnosis remains essential.

patientEducation.summary: Diffuse peripheral nerve disorder, commonly length-dependent, causing sensory, motor and/or autonomic dysfunction. Diabetes is common but metabolic, toxic, nutritional, immune and hereditary causes also occur.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
